espn-603993.headline: Argentina's near misses are Ireland's problem
beats: Argentina have not won since beating Wales in July. They lost to England, South Africa and Australia by seven points or fewer, then drew 28–28 with Australia. They have stopped losing badly. They have not yet started winning.

Ireland last played in July and conceded 40 to New Zealand. They have been third in the world in every ranking since 13 July, and an Argentina win by any margin at the Aviva drops them to fourth, below France.
Tadhg Furlong is cleared to play. A disciplinary committee found he had not grabbed Gavin Coombes in the groin during Leinster's win over Munster.
A week later Ireland host Fiji, who have yet to win a game in the competition. Third place is easier to defend there than to chase.

espn-603994.headline: Italy's last home game ended with England beaten
beats: Since that 23–18 win over England in March, Italy have played four Tests, all away, and lost the lot. In July they conceded 47 to New Zealand and 57 to Australia a week apart.

South Africa lead the Nations Championship on points difference alone, level with New Zealand on 15. Their last outing was a 42–38 loss in Australia, and even a draw in Turin would drop them to second in the world, behind New Zealand.
Gonzalo Quesada calls Italy's position a "Situazione difficile". The cure on offer is a run of home Tests, starting here and then Argentina in Genoa a week later.
The last meeting, on 15 November 2025, was also in Italy, and South Africa won 32–14. Given how the year has gone, Italy would take an 18-point defeat as a decent afternoon.

sources.title: Nations Championship, Quesada alla vigilia delle gare di novembre: "Situazione difficile, ma che piacere ritrovarsi con staff e atleti, misureremo il valore del gruppo"

espn-603995.headline: Scotland score plenty. So does everyone against them
beats: Scotland have scored 28 or more in four of their last five Tests and lost two of them. They let in 42 against South Africa and 43 against Ireland. Even the wins over France and Argentina cost them 40 and 38.
New Zealand lost three straight to South Africa, then put 50 and 43 on Australia with seven tries each time. Last November at Murrayfield, Scotland held them to 25 and still lost 17–25.
A shootout suits nobody in blue. Lose by 16 or more and Scotland drop below Australia in the world rankings, a week before Australia visit Murrayfield.
Next year Scotland go to Dunedin for their first Test in New Zealand in 27 years. The defence has until then to turn up.

sources.title: Scotland to play New Zealand in Dunedin before World Cup — BBC Sport

espn-603996.headline: One point in it last November, one point in it now
beats: Wales beat Japan 24–23 at home on 15 November 2025. They meet again in Cardiff with one win from three each in the Nations Championship, and a single log point between them.

Wales have not played since 18 July, when South Africa beat them 43–0 and they failed to score a try. Japan have been busier. They beat Fiji 20–15 in September, then lost to them 34–28 at home a fortnight ago.

Lose, and Wales fall below Japan and Italy in the world rankings, with Italy yet to take a point in the competition. Wales have called up Macs Page late, and his Scarlets director of rugby, Nigel Davies, thinks he will make his debut soon.
Whoever wins gets no reward next week. Japan go to England, and Wales host New Zealand.

sources.title: Davies backs Page to make Wales debut soon

espn-603997.headline: Fiji's win in Japan earned them nothing on the table
beats: Fiji beat Japan 34–28 on 24 October, avenging September's Pacific Nations Cup final. It was a friendly. In the Nations Championship they are 12th of 12 on zero points, and their pool games include a 73–8 loss to England in July.

France scored six tries in each of their last two games, winning 42–26 in Australia and 42–15 in Japan. Their one pool defeat was by two points in New Zealand. Lose here and they drop to 5th in the world, below England, with South Africa next at home.
Jake White has named four uncapped men in his 35-man squad. One is Nathan Hughes, who won 22 caps for England and now has a second country to try.
France won 34–21 at home last November. With South Africa next, they would take the same again and not ask about the style.

espn-603998.headline: Australia bring ten Tests; England bring a three-day camp
beats: England's last Test was a 31–24 win in Argentina on 18 July. Australia have played 10 since July, while Borthwick's squad got a three-day camp before going back to their clubs, which he calls doing "more of less".
The Australian miles have not all been kind. They beat South Africa 42–38 in September, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October.

Fin Smith started at 10 in all three of England's July Tests and damaged a calf for Northampton. England remain hopeful. They have also called up Charlie Atkinson to sit alongside Marcus Smith and George Ford.
Win and Australia go above England into fifth, which would make all that spare time look expensive.
